question: SGLT2 inhibitors should be stopped for glycaemic benefit when eGFR falls below 45 mL/min/1.73 m², whereas their cardiorenal protective effects can be continued down to lower eGFR thresholds.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. The two eGFR thresholds are distinct: eGFR <45 → inadequate glucose-lowering; eGFR <20–25 → stop for cardiorenal benefit as well (agent-specific).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! For glycaemic efficacy, SGLT2i lose effectiveness below eGFR 45; however, cardiorenal (heart failure / CKD protection) benefits persist to eGFR ~20–25 depending on the agent.
